Zájmena {he}/{his}/{him}/{He}/{His} podle vojáka.
items: a photograph gone soft at the edges
a book with the last pages torn out
a lock of hair in a matchbox
a pack of cards missing the queen of hearts
a child's drawing of a horse
a pocket Bible with a hole in it
a key to a house that is no longer there
enlist: {name} came up the line in the rain with {item} and nothing else. The sergeant wrote {him} down as {rank} and pointed at the mud.
Nobody saw {name} arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in {sector}, and a quiet {archetype} under it.
{name} signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at {sector} took {him} in like it takes everyone: without a word.
They issued {name} a rifle, a spade and a number. {He} kept {item} in {his} breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
{name} arrived with the evening ration party, carrying {item} and a borrowed greatcoat two sizes too big.
The new {archetype} gave {his} name as {name}. The corporal looked at {his} boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
{name} stepped off the supply cart at {sector} and stood very still, listening to the guns as if they were saying {his} name.
Nobody asked {name} why {he} came. Nobody in {sector} asks that. {He} was handed a spade before {he} was handed a rifle.
{name} took the place of a man nobody would talk about. The dugout still had his blanket. {He} kept it folded.
{name} reported to {sector} with {item} sewn into {his} tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
{name} was a {trade} in {home} until the posters went up. {He} came to {sector} with {item}, and within a day the whole bay knew that {he} {quirk}.
In {home}, {name} was a {trade}. In {sector}, {he} is a number and a rifle. {He} has told everyone {he} intends to be a {trade} again.
{name} left {waiting} behind in {home} and came up the line with {item}. The men noticed at once that {he} {quirk}.
The new {archetype} is {name}, once a {trade} from {home}. The corporal asked if a {trade} was any use in a trench. {name} said {he} would find out.
{name} told the sergeant {he} was a {trade}. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed more rain, and put {him} on sentry.
{name} came from {home}, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. {He} talks about all three as if they were people.
{name} arrived at {sector} with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam corrected the cap; the first puddle corrected the rest.
At the depot, {name} had practised answering to {his} name. At {sector}, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
{name} reached {sector} expecting a speech. The welcome consisted of a mug, a space on a bench and directions to the latrine.
The quartermaster asked {name} to sign for the blanket. {He} examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
{name} unpacked {item} at {sector}. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was.
{name} introduced {him}self as a {trade} from {home}. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
On the way to {sector}, {name} tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, {he} was simply glad someone else knew the way.
{name} found a place in {sector} between a snorer and a man who talked in his sleep. The available alternative was under the leak.

daily.text: Rain all night. {name} bailed water out of {sector} with a helmet until {his} hands stopped feeling anything.
{name} wrote a letter home. {He} wrote about the weather. {He} did not write about the rats.
On sentry duty {name} watched the wire for six hours. Twice {he} thought the wire watched back.
A flare lit {place} like noon. {name} counted the seconds until darkness: eleven.
{name} carried duckboards up from the rear all night. {His} shoulders are a map of splinters.
In reserve, {name} slept nine hours in a barn. {He} dreamt of nothing, which was the best part.
{name} traded {item} for two cigarettes and immediately regretted it.
The cook's stew tasted of iron and smoke. {name} ate two helpings anyway.
{name} spent the night underground, listening. Somewhere beneath {place} someone else was digging too.
{name} carried three men out of {sector} on a stretcher. One of them thanked {him}. Two could not.
{name} ran a message through the communication trench under shellfire. The message said: 'Hold.'
{name} lay in the ruins of {place} from dawn to dusk. {He} did not fire once. That is also a kind of victory.
{name} buried two men at the edge of {place} and said the words twice, because the shells interrupted the first time.
{name} cleaned the gun for the fourth time today. The gun is the only thing in the trench that is kept dry.
{name} made soup from what the rats left. The men called it the best soup on the front, and they were not joking.
A shell landed close to {sector}. When the dust settled {name} was still there, holding {item}, laughing without sound.
{name} found a flower growing out of a sandbag. {He} did not tell anyone. {He} checks on it every morning.
A crow sat on the parapet above {name} all afternoon. The men say it chose {him}.
The rain did not stop once. {name} slept standing up, wedged against the wall of {sector}, and dreamt of dry socks.
{name} lost a boot to the mud at {sector}. It took two men and a rifle sling to get it back. The mud kept the sock.
Water rose to the second step of the dugout. {name} moved {item} to the highest shelf and sat beside it like a guard.
Fog so thick that {name} could not see the end of {his} own rifle. Somewhere out there, someone was whistling.
In the fog a figure walked along the parapet of {sector}. When {name} challenged it, there was nobody there.
The fog lifted at noon and {name} saw {place} clearly for the first time. {He} wished it had stayed.
Frost on the wire made it sing in the wind. {name} could not stop listening to it.
{name} woke with {his} hair frozen to the sandbags. The cook brought tea so hot it hurt. Nobody complained.
The mud froze hard overnight. For one morning {name} could walk on top of it, like a man walking on water.
A clear sky. {name} kept {his} head low all day: on clear days the snipers do not miss.
Sun on {sector}. {name} took off {his} boots for the first time in nine days and the whole bay applauded.
Clear night. {name} counted stars until a flare went up and drowned them all.
Lightning lit {place} and {name} saw the enemy wire, the enemy trench, and a man in it looking straight back.
Thunder all night. {name} kept flinching. The old hands said that is how you tell the new ones: they flinch at God.
The east wind brought the smell of the other trenches: smoke, lime and somebody's cooking. {name} was hungry and furious about it.
The wind tore a sheet of corrugated iron off the dugout roof at {sector}. {name} chased it halfway down the communication trench.
{name} spent the night filling sandbags. By dawn {he} could no longer close {his} hands. By noon the shells had emptied half of them again.
{name} had a letter from home. {He} read it four times and then once more out loud, for the men who never get any.
A rat stole {name}'s cheese ration while {he} watched. {He} let it. The rat looked hungrier.
{name} was on wiring party in no man's land. Every time a flare went up {he} froze like a scarecrow. It worked.
{name} lost at cards to the corporal and now owes him a week of tobacco and one favour, unspecified.
Rumour reached {sector} that the war would be over by spring. {name} has heard it before. So has everyone.
{name} carved {his} initials into the trench wall next to a hundred others. Some of them are only half finished.
{name} spent the afternoon delousing {his} shirt over a candle. The lice won on points.
{name} sang under {his} breath on sentry. Across the wire, very quietly, somebody sang the next line.
A shell hit the latrine at {sector}. Nobody was hurt. {name} says it was the best day of the war.
Officers came to inspect {sector}. {name} polished {his} buttons with mud, which is the only polish there is.
{name} found an old map of {place} from before the war. There was a school on it, and an orchard. {He} looked for them. {He} did not find them.
{name} turned a year older today. The bay sang for {him}, badly, and the cook found a candle.
{name} saw a hare run the whole length of no man's land and nobody on either side fired at it.
{name} stood to at dawn with the rest of {sector}, bayonet fixed, staring into the grey. Nothing came. Nothing came yesterday, either.
Listening post, three in the morning. {name} heard boots, then whispering, then nothing. Just a fox, the corporal said. {He} did not sleep afterwards.
A trench raid went out from {sector}. {name} waited at the gap in the wire, counting heads as they came back.
{name} hauled ammunition boxes up the communication trench all night. {His} back filed a formal complaint.
{name} repaired a collapsed traverse at {sector} with sandbags, boards and language not fit for letters home.
Behind the lines {name} had a bath in a beer vat with eleven other men. The water was brown before {he} got in.
In the reserve billet {name} played football against the sappers. The ball was a sandbag stuffed with straw. The sappers cheated.
{name} drew the counter-mine plans by candlelight. Below {place} the earth is now a maze, and {he} knows every turn.
{name} set a charge under the enemy listening post. Then {he} waited all night for an order that did not come.
{name} splinted a broken leg with a rifle and two puttees. The patient asked if {he} was a real doctor. {He} said yes. {He} was lying.
The aid post ran out of morphine at four. {name} held a boy's hand until six. Then {he} went back for the next one.
{name} ran six messages in one night. The last one was a request for more runners.
{name} took the long way round {place} because the short way had a sniper on it. The long way had two.
{name} spent the day watching one loophole in the enemy line. At dusk a periscope rose in it. {He} let it go. Tomorrow.
{name} moved {his} hide three times today. Snipers who stay in one place do not stay anywhere for long.
The machine gun jammed at the worst moment. {name} cleared it with a bent nail and words the chaplain pretended not to hear.
{name} fired three short bursts at nothing to keep the enemy honest. The enemy fired three back to keep {him} honest too.
The telephone wire to {sector} was cut by shelling four times. {name} crawled out and spliced it four times.
{name} sent a pigeon back to headquarters. The pigeon came back two hours later. {name} took it personally.
{name} flashed a lamp signal to the battery behind the ridge. The answer came back: a single word, misspelled.
The cook's fire went out in the rain. {name} relit it under {his} own greatcoat and served stew that tasted of wool.
{name} carried hot tea up to the front line in petrol cans. Everyone could taste the petrol. Everyone drank it.
{name} held a service in a shell hole. Eleven men came. Two of them had never prayed before. Both of them asked for another.
{name} wrote letters for men who could not write, and some for men who could but did not know the words.
{name} studied the trench map until the candle died, then walked {sector} in the dark to learn it by heart.
{name} had orders to attack at dawn. {He} wrote back asking for artillery first. The orders were cancelled. Nobody knows which of {his} words did it.
{name} censored the men's letters tonight. {He} crossed out the place names and left in all the love.
{name} wrote to {waiting}. {He} did not mention the shelling. {He} mentioned the stars.
Someone in {sector} asked {name} about {home}. {He} talked for an hour. Nobody interrupted.
{name}'s hands still remember being a {trade}'s hands. Today they mended a broken duckboard as if it were the most important job in the world.
The men have learned that {name} {quirk}. Tonight it made them laugh, which was worth a great deal.
A letter reached {name} from {home}. The streets there still have names. {He} read them out loud, one by one.
{name} dreamt {he} was back in {home}, working as a {trade}. {He} woke to rain and said nothing all morning.
{name} {quirk}. Today, under fire at {place}, that habit was the only steady thing in {sector}.
Asked what {he} will do after the war, {name} said: 'Be a {trade} in {home}. And never complain about anything, ever again.'
A replacement turned out to be from {home} too. {name} and the newcomer argued about the same bakery for half the night.
{name} thought about {waiting} on sentry tonight, and the cold felt a little further away.
The corporal found out {name} used to be a {trade}. {name} has been doing two jobs ever since.
{name} found a shirt button in the bread. {He} ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful.
The parcel for {name} contained six left socks. By supper, {he} had found three men willing to trade.
{name} tried to describe the smell of {home} and got as far as the bakery. Then the ration cart arrived.
A borrowed pencil wore down while {name} was writing home. The last line is twice as large as the first.
{name} shaved using a spoon for a mirror. One side looks ready for inspection. The other looks ready for winter.
The bread was divided with a ruler. {name} received the smallest piece and the job of looking after the ruler.
{name} spent an hour repairing a pocket. Nothing goes in it now without a careful inspection.
Someone had labelled the water bucket 'Soup'. {name} changed it back after lunch, too late to settle the argument.
The shelling stopped while {name} was counting between impacts. {He} reached the next number anyway, then waited a long time before moving.
A newspaper reached {name} with the corner torn off. The war was going well, according to half a sentence.
{name} dreamt of missing a train. Waking up here seemed an unreasonable punishment for it.
The blanket exchange left {name} with a better blanket and a reputation for sharp dealing. The previous owner wants a rematch.
{name} tried writing with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will require imagination.
{name} found a clean patch on the table and put {his} bread on it. Someone immediately asked to borrow the patch.
The next dugout has acquired a doorbell. {name} went to inspect it. It is a spoon tied to an empty tin.
{name} was asked what {he} wanted after the war. A chair, {he} said. After some thought: a chair nobody else was using.
{name} heard wire rattle beyond the parapet. At relief, the next sentry was told exactly where and asked not to dismiss it.
{name} drew the street leading into {home}. There was no room for the last house, so {he} used the back of the page.
The men argued about whether fish sleep. {name} said yes, and was made to explain how anyone could tell.
A shot struck the sandbag beside {name}. {He} crouched down and discovered that the hands could shake while still doing everything required.
{name} saved half a biscuit for later. Later turned out to be six minutes away.
The cook asked for an honest opinion. {name} asked whether second helpings depended on the answer.
{name} brushed dried mud from a letter and uncovered one more word: 'soon'. {He} wished the sentence around it had survived.
The patrol returned one at a time. {name} held the entrance clear and counted until the corporal said that was everyone.
{name} wrote a list of things to buy on leave. It began with socks and ended with a meal nobody could call a ration.
A new pair of laces made {name}'s boots look briefly respectable. The effect lasted until {he} stood up.
{name} waited at the fire step while a flare burned out. The pale shape beyond the wire resolved into a sack, exactly where the sack had always been.
The parcel contained a comb. {name} has hardly any hair left after the last haircut, but accepted the encouragement.
An unexploded shell lay beside the approach trench. {name} helped divert the carrying party and was glad to leave its inspection to someone else.
An empty jam tin became {name}'s cup. The first drink tasted faintly of strawberries. {He} took smaller sips than usual.
{name} remembered the tune but not the words. Six volunteers supplied six different songs, none of them an improvement.
The warning to check masks reached {name} during supper. {He} put the bread down carefully and did not finish it until the all-clear.
{name} washed {his} face and was asked whether headquarters was visiting. Apparently cleanliness requires an explanation.
{name} borrowed a book with three readers already waiting. For once, everyone was impatient about something other than relief.
The lice inspection interrupted a fierce argument about politics. {name} observed that at least one enemy had been positively identified.
{name} heard a man laugh beyond the enemy parapet. The sound was ordinary enough to be more unsettling than a shot.
{name} tried to remember the sound of the bell in {home}. Every version came out sounding like the ration bell.
A section of parapet collapsed near {name}. The repairs began as soon as the dust settled, with one man watching while the others worked.
{name} received a photograph taken outside the family home. {He} studied the unfamiliar curtains longer than the faces.
{name} was halfway through a story when the listener fell asleep. {He} took it as a useful service rendered.
Someone asked {name} to wake them in ten minutes. {He} spent all ten worrying about how to measure them.
{name} came off watch unable to remember whether the last hour had been long or short. {He} remembered every movement in one patch of wire.
The company barber offered a choice of styles. {name} asked to see the second one. The barber laughed.
{name} caught {him}self counting portions before counting people. {He} started again.
The trench wall shook against {name}'s shoulder during the bombardment. {He} pressed both feet into the boards and waited for the next impact.
A story about a goat travelled through three dugouts and reached {name} as a story about a general. The ending was unchanged.
{name} checked the safety catch three times before handing over the post. The replacement noticed and checked it once more.
{name} spent the evening teaching a recruit to sew. The recruit pricked a finger and accused the needle of taking sides.
Shellfire stopped the carrying party at a trench junction. {name} waited beneath a load that grew heavier with every minute.
{name} sharpened a pencil with great care and then could not think what to write. {He} put the date at the top anyway.
{name} opened a parcel addressed in an unfamiliar hand. Inside was a note explaining that the usual letter writer had hurt a wrist. {He} read that note first.
{name} traded a cigarette for a pinch of salt. Supper was better; the discussion of the exchange rate was worse.
A pocket watch passed along the bench so everyone could set the time. {name} has no watch, but looked carefully all the same.
A stretcher party needed the passage. {name} backed into a recess with an ammunition box and held it there until the last bearer passed.
{name} tried to sketch a horse from memory. The result has been accepted by the dugout as a very good dog.
{name} brought replacement sandbags forward and found the damage worse than the message had said. The party sent back for another load.
{name} finished a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.
The telephone failed during the shelling. {name} watched the runner leave with the written orders, then listened for the telephone to ring again.
{name} kept a seat for someone fetching supper. Holding it against three hungry men proved harder than expected.
{name} counted the stitches in a darned sock while waiting for orders. Whoever repaired it had used three colours of wool.
The dugout roof dripped into {name}'s mug. {He} moved the mug. The roof found another way.
{name} stretched a scrap of canvas over the letters. Everything else could get wet first.
Rain washed the chalk names from the trench signs. {name} spent the evening directing strangers past the same junction.
{name} tipped water from a boot and a small beetle climbed out. At least one passenger had enjoyed the crossing.
{name} followed a cough through the fog and found the ration party stuck at a junction. For once, a cough improved supper.
Fog hid the far end of {sector}. {name} kept counting the bays to avoid walking past the dugout.
A familiar voice came out of the fog in the wrong direction. {name} waited for the password before answering.
{name} watched fog gather on the wire until every strand carried beads of water. The sentry beside {him} called it expensive fencing.
{name} warmed the ink bottle inside {his} tunic. The letter began only when the ink agreed to move.
The bread had frozen at the edges. {name} held it near the stove and defended the space with both elbows.
{name} tried to fold a frozen groundsheet. It objected loudly enough to wake the next sleeper.
Frost made each footprint distinct. {name} followed a trail to the missing ration sack and found the quartermaster sitting on it.
{name} aired a blanket in the sunshine and stood beside it, enjoying the same treatment.
The sky stayed clear above {sector}. {name} watched a small cloud form and quietly hoped it would bring friends.
{name} held a letter up to the daylight to read the faint last lines. They were only a shopping list, written on reused paper.
In the clear evening, {name} could see smoke rising far beyond the guns. Somewhere, supper was being cooked in a proper kitchen.
A gust blew rain under the dugout door. {name} moved the boots indoors, then remembered they were already indoors.
{name} braced a loose roof board while the storm passed. Every conversation had to wait until {he} could lower both arms.
Thunder shook dust from the beams over {name}. The man beside {him} asked whether the sky had the correct range.
The storm put out the lamp twice. On the third attempt, {name} and two others formed a very irritated windbreak.
Wind kept turning the pages of {name}'s letter. {He} held them down with a biscuit and finished with crumbs in the ink.
{name} spent the afternoon chasing a cap that stopped moving whenever {he} stopped chasing it.
A loose strip of canvas snapped above {name}'s bunk. {He} tied it down and received thanks from six apparently sleeping men.
The wind carried away the last words of every order. {name} waited until the corporal came closer before picking up anything heavy.
{name} cleaned grit from the rifle bolt with a scrap of cloth. The scrap was once the clean part of a shirt.
The new recruit kept closing both eyes to aim. {name} spent the afternoon helping until one eye stayed open.
{name} checked each belt by lamplight. A cartridge seated badly was enough to start the whole inspection again.
The gun team argued about who had carried the heaviest load. {name} suggested exchanging loads. The argument ended immediately.
{name} measured a replacement beam three times. The passage was narrow enough to punish optimism.
A pump handle came off in {name}'s hands. {He} repaired it while the water rose around {his} ankles.
A patient apologised for bleeding on {name}'s sleeve. {He} asked the patient to concentrate on staying awake instead.
{name} labelled the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, {he} could find everything without looking.
{name} delivered an urgent message and waited while the recipient searched every pocket for a pencil to acknowledge it.
A new trench junction cost {name} ten minutes. {He} marked the correct turn with a broken spoon on the return journey.
{name} noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. {He} watched it until dusk and wrote down the change.
A beetle crawled across {name}'s sleeve during the long wait. {He} could do nothing about it without giving away the position.
{name} tested the telephone and heard someone at headquarters chewing. The line was pronounced perfectly clear.
{name} taught a replacement to recognise letters by sound. By supper, the table had become an unofficial Morse key.
{name} counted the ladles in the pot against the men in the queue. The final serving took some careful scraping.
Someone returned an empty pot polished with bread. {name} accepted it as a review.
A man asked {name} to sit nearby without saying anything. {He} stayed until the man fell asleep.
{name} conducted a service beside a ration store. The men sang quietly so the sleepers behind the wall could rest.
{name} checked the duty roster and found the same names on the worst shifts. {He} fetched a fresh sheet of paper.
A report called the trench satisfactory. {name} invited its author to spend the night there before signing it.
{name} lifted the trench periscope and found a spider across the mirror. For one startled second, the enemy seemed enormous.
The listening post reported scraping beyond the wire. {name} waited through an hour of it before a loose stake was found.
A flare caught {name} halfway through a yawn on the fire step. {He} stayed still until {his} jaw ached.
{name} checked the firing step after the shelling. The wall had moved; the familiar place for one foot was gone.
{name} passed ration containers down a chain of hands. By the time supper reached the front, every man smelled of it.
Two carrying parties met in the narrow trench. {name} helped negotiate the passing of an ammunition box and a very large kettle.
{name} stacked spare duckboards beside the junction. Within an hour, the stack had become a bench, a table and an argument.
The relief column arrived early. {name} made room in the shelter by moving everything except the men already asleep.
{name} found a chair in the billet and sat down carefully, as though it might be reserved for someone of higher rank.
The village shop had three kinds of soap. {name} stood at the counter far longer than the purchase required.
{name} watched a woman sweep her doorstep. {He} had forgotten that dirt could be removed permanently from anywhere.
In the billet, {name} woke at the usual watch hour. For several minutes, nobody could persuade {him} to go back to sleep.
{name} tried to remember the price of a loaf in {home}. Three different answers seemed right, depending on how far back {he} thought.
A parcel arrived tied with blue ribbon. {name} gave the contents away and kept the ribbon to mark a page.
{name} borrowed a magnifying glass to read cramped handwriting. The urgently needed word turned out to be 'cabbage'.
The section held a competition for the worst joke. {name} won before reaching the end of {his} entry.
{name} was promised a surprise at supper. It was an extra potato. {He} accepted the surprise with proper ceremony.
An old advertisement showed a spotless man smoking beside a fireplace. {name} added a leak above the man's head in pencil.
{name} drew a line on the bench to settle an argument about space. Everyone obeyed it until the broadest man returned from duty.
A child had enclosed a riddle in a parcel for {name}. The answer was on the back. {He} kept the dugout guessing until supper.
{name} took stock of {his} pockets: string, crumbs, a pencil and no sign of the button {he} was looking for.
Someone had used a newspaper to wrap the onions. {name} read a theatre review while peeling supper.
{name} mended a split glove with pale thread. The repair makes one finger look as though it has been promoted.
A sneeze blew dust off the shelf above {name}. This caused another sneeze and a discussion about moving the shelf.
{name} has learnt to recognise the ration cart by its squeaking wheel. A different squeak caused considerable disappointment this afternoon.
The cook borrowed {name}'s mug to measure flour. Getting it back involved waiting for the dough, the baking and the cook's memory.
{name} kept a tally of complaints about the tea. The tally ended when somebody asked whether {he} was volunteering to make it.
A loose thread in {name}'s blanket proved longer than expected. By the time {he} stopped pulling, the repair needed explaining.
{name} read a letter that said the neighbour had married again. The whole dugout wanted the missing first half of the story.
The new soap slipped into the wash bucket. {name} recovered it by touch and then had to wash again.
{name} measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.
A man asked {name} to describe {home} without mentioning the weather. {He} began with the steepest street and ended with the cheapest lunch.
{name} polished a spoon until {he} could see a small, bent version of {his} face. It looked unimpressed with supper too.
The kettle lid rattled whenever the conversation stopped. {name} put a folded cloth beneath it and immediately missed the noise.
{name} tried to dry a page near the stove. The paper survived, but the message now has the smell of toasted bread.
A scrap of newspaper announced a sale of garden furniture. {name} calculated how many months' pay a comfortable afternoon might cost.
{name} caught a falling mug with {his} foot. Saving the mug was impressive; retrieving the foot without spilling it required assistance.
{name} offered to read the newspaper aloud. The audience requested the advertisements first, then the racing, and finally the war.
A parcel contained a bar of chocolate broken into uneven pieces. {name} closed {his} eyes while someone else distributed them.
{name} found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. {He} folded it along the original creases.
{name} laughed at something nobody else had heard. Asked to share it, {he} admitted remembering a conversation from years ago.
A borrowed towel came back cleaner than when {name} lent it. {He} is considering lending out the rest of the washing.
{name} tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, {he} was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived.
The last of the jam was shared by [passing the tin around|scraping it onto a biscuit|adding hot water and calling it a drink]. {name} approved the method.
{name} put [a flat stone|an empty tin|a folded ration label] under a short table leg. Supper stopped sliding toward the corporal.
{name} offered [a biscuit|a length of string|a spare button] for a better place near the stove. The offer was refused with surprising dignity.

promotion: For keeping {his} head when others lost theirs at {place}, {name} was promoted to {rank}.
The old {oldRank} did not come back from the wire. {name} wears {his} stripes now: {rank}.
{name} brought back a wounded man and a lost machine gun from {place} in one trip. {He} is {rank} now.
Nobody else in {sector} wanted the stripes. {name} said yes. {rank}.
The colonel asked who held the line at {place} last night. Every finger pointed at {name}. {rank}.
{name} was made {rank}. {He} celebrated by sleeping four hours in a row.
{name} was promoted to {rank}. The first request addressed to the new rank concerned a blocked drain.
The order named {name} as {rank}. {He} read it twice, then asked who would take over {his} watch.
{name} received the rank of {rank} and a stack of unfinished paperwork. The congratulations lasted less time than the paperwork.
Promoted to {rank}, {name} had to settle an argument {he} had been happily taking part in five minutes earlier.
{name} is {rank} now. At supper, a recruit waited for {him} to sit before taking a place. {He} noticed.
The promotion to {rank} reached {name} on a creased slip of paper. {He} smoothed it and put it with the letters from home.
{name} was made {rank} after keeping the section together under fire. {He} asked that the rest of the section be mentioned too.
{name} accepted promotion to {rank}. Later, {he} practised giving the morning orders quietly enough not to wake the dugout.
wounded: Shrapnel at {place}. {name} walked to the aid post on {his} own feet and asked for a cigarette before the stitches.
{name} was caught by gas at {sector}. {He} coughs in {his} sleep but swears {he} will be back on the line within the week.
A rifle grenade burst above {sector}. {name} took a splinter in the arm and refused to leave until the next man was bandaged.
{name} was buried by a shell at {place}. They dug {him} out after twenty minutes, deaf in one ear and still holding {item}.
Trench foot. {name} can no longer feel {his} toes and the medical officer has ordered {him} to the rear, swearing at the mud.
{name} was hit by a sniper at {place}. The bullet went through {his} shoulder and, somehow, missed everything that mattered.
A fever swept through {sector}. {name} was carried out shaking and talking to people who were not there.
Barbed wire at {place} opened {name}'s leg from knee to ankle. {He} limped back in carrying the wire-cutters, as ordered.
A splinter caught {name} at {sector}. At the aid post, {he} was more upset about the ruined sleeve than the dressing beneath it.
{name} reached the aid post with a wounded hand held against {his} chest. Someone else had to unfasten the buttons.
Flying masonry struck {name} at {place}. The stretcher jolted over every familiar board on the way out.
{name} took a bullet in the leg at {sector}. {He} passed the rifle to the next man before allowing the bearers to lift {him}.
The blast at {place} threw {name} against the trench wall. At the aid post, the questions sounded far away.
{name} was wounded during shelling at {sector}. The last thing {he} asked before leaving was whether the relief had arrived.
A fragment struck {name}'s shoulder. The dressing covered a pocket {he} kept trying to reach, until an orderly retrieved its contents.
{name} was carried from {place} with a wounded leg. {He} apologised whenever the bearers had to stop.
recovered: {name} is back from the field hospital, thinner and quieter, with {item} still in {his} pocket.
{name} came back to {sector} with a new scar and an old joke. The bay was glad of both.
The field hospital let {name} go. {He} came back up the line on foot because the lorry would not wait.
{name} returned from hospital carrying letters, chocolate and rumours, and handed out all three.
Back with {his} platoon, {name} found that someone had kept {his} place on the fire step. Nobody admitted who.
{name} returned from hospital and found a new face beside the bunk. The old argument about shelf space resumed immediately.
Declared fit, {name} reported back to {sector}. The familiar smell reached {him} before the familiar voices.
{name} came back from hospital with a clean shirt. The men admired it from a respectful distance.
The medical officer cleared {name} for duty. At {sector}, someone quietly moved a pack off {his} usual seat.
{name} returned with instructions to take care. The corporal read them, looked around {sector}, and folded them carefully.
Back from hospital, {name} distributed messages from other recovering men. For an hour, the dugout sounded like a railway waiting room.
{name} rejoined {sector} carrying a borrowed book from the ward. Returning it has become a reason to survive the next leave application.
{name} came back fit for duty and discovered the section had changed the recipe for its tea. {He} demanded an explanation.
fallen: {name} fell at {place}. They found {item} in {his} pocket and sent it home with a letter that said {he} was brave. It was true.
The wire at {place} took {name}. {His} friends in {sector} carved {his} name into a duckboard so the mud would remember {him}.
{name} went over the top at {place} and did not come back. The roll was called twice. Nobody answered for {him}.
A shell found {name} in the dugout at {sector}. The men put {his} helmet on a cross by the road. It is still there.
{name} died at the aid post at dawn, holding {item}. The chaplain says {he} was smiling. The chaplain says that about everyone, but this time it was true.
{name} was lost in the mine explosion under {place}. There was nothing to bury. They buried {his} name instead.
{name} was killed at {place}. At supper, someone began to set out another mug, then put it back.
A shell killed {name} at {sector}. The letter in {his} kit was finished except for the signature.
{name} fell during the fighting at {place}. The corporal checked the spelling before sending the report.
{name} died at the aid post. An orderly recorded {his} name, gathered the personal effects and sat still for a moment before the next stretcher.
{name} was killed at {sector}. A small debt owed to {him} was written off without discussion.
The fighting at {place} claimed {name}. Nobody wanted the space on the shelf, though everyone had wanted it yesterday.
{name} did not survive the bombardment. The section collected the letters from {his} pack and tied them with their original string.
{name} fell at {place}. A man who barely knew {him} remembered being lent a needle and asked to help write home.
heir: {name} came to the front because {his} {relation} {prevName} never came home. {He} carries {item}.
The papers say {name}. The sergeant says {he} has {his} {relation}'s eyes. {prevName}'s eyes. Nobody in {sector} argues.
A letter came with {name}: "I am {prevName}'s {relation}. I have come to finish what {he} started." Nobody had the heart to tell {him} it never finishes.
{name} took the same post at {sector} where {prevName} stood. {He} found {his} {relation}'s initials carved in the wall and put {his} own beneath them.
The House of {family} sent another. {name}, {relation} of {prevName}, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence.
{name} arrived carrying the family name of {prevName}. The corporal asked how to pronounce {his} first name, and waited for the answer.
The House of {family} sent {name} after {prevName}. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks.
{name} asked about {prevName} on arriving at {sector}. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. {He} asked for another.
{name} put {item} beside the bunk. Someone who had known {prevName} helped clear the shelf without saying why.
{name} had heard about {prevName}'s courage. At {sector}, {he} also heard about the snoring, the cards and the terrible handwriting.
The papers connected {name} to {prevName}. The men took longer to learn {name}'s own habits, but they made the effort.
{name} joined {sector} under the shadow of {prevName}'s name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one.
Another member of the House of {family} reached the line: {name}. {He} asked where {prevName} had slept, then chose a different corner.
missing: {name} went out with a patrol to {place} and did not come back with it. {He} is listed as missing. The men leave {his} rations untouched.
After the raid on {place}, {name} was not at the roll call. Somebody saw {him} in a shell hole. Somebody else says that was someone else.
{name} took a message across {place} at dusk. The message arrived. {name} did not.
{name} was absent when the patrol returned from {place}. The corporal checked the list against the faces, then checked it again.
The last report placed {name} near {place}. By evening, no later report had arrived. Missing.
After the shelling at {sector}, nobody could account for {name}. {His} kit remains beside the bunk.
{name} failed to return from the wire. A search found tracks leading into churned ground and nothing certain beyond it.
At roll call, {name}'s place stayed empty. Someone said another section might have taken {him} in. A runner was sent to ask.
The party came back from {place} by different routes. By dawn, everyone had been accounted for except {name}.
{name} was last seen moving toward cover at {place}. No one agrees which shelter. The report lists {him} as missing.
The relief reached {sector} without {name}. {His} name was added to a list the corporal kept separate from the dead.
returned: {name} crawled back into {sector} at dawn after two nights in a shell hole at {place}, covered in mud and carrying {item}. {He} asked if {he} had missed breakfast.
The sentry nearly shot {name} coming in through the wire. {He} had been lost in the fog at {place}, living on rainwater and stubbornness.
{name} turned up at a neighbouring battalion, having walked the wrong way for a day and a half. {He} came home to {sector} with three new friends and no explanation.
{name} came back to {sector} after sheltering with another unit. {He} brought a note confirming the story and a borrowed mug to return.
The missing report was still on the desk when {name} walked in. The clerk crossed it out hard enough to tear the paper.
{name} returned after being cut off near {place}. {He} knew the password, but could barely make the sentry hear it.
Found with a party from another section, {name} was guided back to {sector}. The relief on the corporal's face lasted until the lecture began.
{name} returned by a trench nobody thought passable. {He} asked for water before explaining how little of it was still a trench.
A sentry called down that {name} was at the wire. Three men went to help before anyone gave an order.
{name} reappeared at {sector} carrying a scrap of map from another unit. The route home had been drawn over somebody's shopping list.
{name} came back exhausted, having waited in cover until the way cleared. {He} slept through the argument about who had worried most.
comrade: {a} and {b} shared the last tin of bully beef in the bay, counting the bites out loud to keep it fair.
{a} kept watch so that {b} could sleep. Then {bs} kept watch so that {as} could. Neither slept.
{a} taught {b} to play the harmonica. The bay has asked them both, formally, to stop.
{a} pulled {b} out of a flooded shell hole at {place}. Neither of them has mentioned it since. Both of them remember.
{a} and {b} argued all night about whose home town has the better beer. The argument has been adjourned until after the war.
{a} cut {b}'s hair with a bayonet and a cracked mirror. It is not good. It is, however, short.
{a} wrote a letter for {b}'s mother, because {bs} could not find the words. {bs} signed it.
{a} and {b} carved a chessboard into an ammunition box. The pieces are bullets, buttons and one very patient beetle.
{a} and {b} made a pact on sentry tonight: whoever gets home first visits the other's family. They shook on it with frozen hands.
{a} saw {b} freeze on the fire step at {place}. {as} said nothing, just stood closer. It was enough.
{a} and {b} divided a parcel using the lid of a tin as scales. The final crumb required a second opinion.
{a} held the mirror while {b} shaved. The arrangement survived the shaving but not the comments.
{a} and {b} compared drawings of home. Both drawings included a kitchen table larger than the house.
{a} lent {b} a pencil. The returned pencil came wrapped in a scrap of paper marked 'One good turn'.
{a} and {b} carried a kettle through three narrow traverses without spilling a drop. Applause at the destination caused the accident.
{a} repaired the strap on {b}'s pack. Payment was a biscuit and a promise to stop mentioning the haircut.
{a} and {b} tried to invent a new card game. The rules became clearer only after the tobacco stakes were removed.
{a} and {b} sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At relief, the next watch was told it had been a good hour.
enemy: At {place}, {a} of the {af} and {b} of the {bf} traded insults across the wire for an hour. By the end they were trading recipes.
{a} ({af}) and {b} ({bf}) met in the same shell hole at {place} during a raid. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
{b} of the {bf} threw a tin of tobacco into the {af} trench with a note: "for the one who sings". {a} kept the tin.
{a} had {b} of the {bf} in {his} sights at {place} for a long second. {b} was lighting a pipe. {a} let the match burn all the way down.
A football came over the parapet from the {bf} side with {b}'s name scratched on it. {a} kicked it back. It did not come again.
On a quiet night {a} ({af}) and {b} ({bf}) called out their names across no man's land, just to hear another voice. Now each knows exactly who is out there.
At {place}, {a} of the {af} and {b} of the {bf} fired at the same loose sheet of metal. The wind kept winning.
{a} ({af}) and {b} ({bf}) spotted the same abandoned cart near {place}. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was.
During a lull at {place}, {a} called across from the {af} line. {b} answered from the {bf} side with a convincing imitation of an officer. Both trenches went quiet.
{a} of the {af} and {b} of the {bf} watched a broken branch near {place} all morning. Neither side could afford to assume it was only a branch.
A shouted challenge from {a} ({af}) reached {b} ({bf}) at {place}. The answer was lost beneath the guns. The challenge was not repeated.
At {place}, {a} and {b} exchanged rifle shots until a shell burst between the positions. For a while, both rifles remained silent.
{a} of the {af} spotted {b} of the {bf} repairing a parapet at {place}. A warning shot brought the repair to an abrupt halt.
A bucket appeared above the {bf} parapet at {place}. {a} fired; {b} pulled the bucket down. A sign later appeared: 'Water costs enough already.'

steps: A rat has started sitting on the ammunition box next to {name}'s bunk. {He} has named it {pet}.
{pet} the rat now waits for {name} at stand-to every morning. {He} shares crumbs with it. The corporal calls this desertion of rations.
{pet} ran squealing out of the dugout at three in the morning. {name} followed, cursing, seconds before a shell came through the roof. {He} owes {pet} {his} life.
{name} has not seen {pet} for two days. {He} tells everyone rats come and go. {He} still leaves crumbs on the box.
{name} got a letter from {love}. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. {He} read that page most.
{name} wrote back to {love} and tore it up three times. The fourth version says almost nothing, which is how {he} knows it is the right one.
No post for {name} this week. {He} checks the sack anyway, every day, and pretends {he} was only looking for tobacco.
A parcel from {love}: socks, a cake gone hard as a brick, and a pressed flower. {name} ate the cake and kept the flower in {item}'s place.
A one-eyed crow landed on the parapet above {name}. The men named it {crow} and said it had chosen {him}.
{crow} the crow follows {name} along the trench now. When {crow} flies off, men duck. They are usually right to.
Somebody in {sector} wanted to shoot {crow} for the pot. {name} stood in front of the rifle. The matter has been dropped.
A muddy dog crawled into {sector} through the wire. {name} gave it half {his} bread. It has not left {his} side since. The men call it {dog}.
{dog} has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. {name} is very proud. {dog} is mainly proud of the biscuits.
{dog} barked at nothing in the dark at four in the morning, and kept barking. A raiding party was twenty yards from the wire. {sector} was ready for them.
{name} hummed an old song from home on sentry. From the other side of the wire, very faintly, someone hummed it back.
{name} sang the first verse tonight, out loud. The other side sang the second. Nobody fired for an hour.
An officer heard about the singing and forbade it. Tonight {name} only whistled the first bar. Across the wire, someone whistled the last.

stranger: a woman in a white dress
two small boys on a bench
an old man with a dog

steps: {name} found a photograph in the mud of no man's land: {stranger}, and a name on the back that is not from {his} side of the wire.
{name} keeps the photograph in {his} pocket next to {item}. {He} says {he} will give it back after the war. Nobody asks to whom.
{name} left the photograph on a stake in the wire at {place}, wrapped in oilcloth. In the morning it was gone. In its place: a single cigarette.

stake: a pocket watch that does not work

steps: {name} won {stake} at cards from a lance corporal in {sector}. The lance corporal wants a rematch.
Rematch. {name} lost everything {he} won, plus {item}. The whole dugout watched.
Third game, by candlelight, with the shelling for a clock. {name} won back {item} and nothing else. {He} says that was all {he} was playing for.
{name} pressed {his} ear to the tunnel wall under {place} and heard it: tapping. Someone is digging toward {him}.
The tapping under {place} is closer. {name} and two others work in silence, in socks, by the light of one candle.
{name} broke through into the enemy gallery at dawn. It was empty. A lamp was still warm. {He} blew it out and placed the charge.
The mine under {place} went up at noon. The whole front felt it. {name} sat at the tunnel mouth afterwards and did not speak until dark.
There is a sniper across the way the men call {foe}. Three helmets went up on sticks today. {foe} hit all three. {name} watched where the shots came from.
{name} lay in the ruins of {place} all day. {foe} did not fire once. Neither did {name}. Both of them know.
At dusk a glint from the ridge. {name} fired once. The front has been quiet ever since, and nobody talks about {foe} any more.
{name} carried in {boy}, who lied about his age to enlist. {boy} kept asking whether his mother would be told.
{boy} has a fever. {name} sits with him after every shift and reads to him from a book with the last pages missing.
{boy} was put on the hospital train today, alive. He gave {name} a button from his tunic. {name} wears it on {his} own.
{name} learned that {prize} is stored in the cellar at battalion headquarters. {He} has been making careful drawings.
{name} volunteered for a supply run to headquarters. {He} came back with exactly what was ordered and a suspiciously large greatcoat.
The whole of {sector} ate well tonight. {prize} has been reported missing. {name} has been reported as a very good cook.
The line to the battery keeps going dead at the same spot near {place}. {name} suspects it is not the shelling.
{name} crawled out along the wire at night and found the break: neat, cut, recent. Someone is listening in.
{name} laid a second line, deep, by a different route, and left the old one live with false orders on it. Tomorrow the enemy shells an empty farm.
{name} started keeping a diary in the back of a field service book. First entry: "Still here."
{name}'s diary, day nine: "Still here. Rain. A rat called the Major. Nothing else worth writing, which is the point."
{name} read {his} diary from the start tonight and laughed at how frightened {he} was back then. Then {he} stopped laughing and wrote: "Still here."
{name} borrowed a serial novel from a newspaper bundle. The instalment ends with a locked door and a pistol shot. The next issue is missing.
{name} has asked three carrying parties for the next instalment. So far, the search has produced racing results and an advertisement for boots.
The dugout has begun inventing endings to {name}'s story. The cook's version involves an inheritance; the corporal's involves a disciplinary hearing.
The missing instalment reached {name}. The explanation was so poor that the dugout voted to keep the cook's ending.

record: a waltz with a scratched introduction
a march played slightly too slowly
an operatic duet nobody can translate

steps: A supply man offered {name} a damaged gramophone in exchange for help unloading. {He} accepted before asking whether there were any records.
{name} coaxed the gramophone into turning. It plays {record}, but something knocks once every revolution.
The gramophone stopped knocking after {name} tightened a screw. The dugout applauded the repair halfway through {record}, spoiling the best part.
{name} passed the gramophone to the next section with a note about the screw. By evening, {record} could be heard faintly through the wall.
{name} began a chess game by post with a friend at home. {He} copied the opening move onto the corner of an ordinary letter.
The reply to {name}'s chess move arrived with a complaint about the weather at home. {His} opponent has taken a pawn and apologised for nothing.
{name} asked the dugout for advice on the next move. Three men disagreed so fiercely that a second board had to be drawn.
{name} received a letter announcing checkmate. The dugout insists the position was copied incorrectly. {He} has written back asking for another game.
{name} found a blank menu card and wrote the evening ration on it in elaborate handwriting. The bread became 'Bread, in the Army Manner'.
{name}'s menu now circulates before supper. Someone has requested a wine list. The water bucket has been given a vintage.
An officer asked who was writing the menus. {name} admitted it and waited. The officer asked for a copy to send home.
{name} retired the menu after running out of grand names for turnips. The final card reads 'The Usual', underlined twice.
A recruit asked {name} how to write an address. {He} brought paper and began with the largest letters on a ration label.
{name} and the recruit have reached whole words. Lessons take place beside the stove, with spelling corrections from people pretending not to listen.
The recruit wrote a first short letter without {name}'s help. {He} was allowed to check the envelope, but not the contents.
A reply arrived for the recruit. {name} listened while it was read aloud, slowly, without once supplying a word.
{name} received a parcel meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside were {gift}. {He} put everything back and kept the wrapping.
The parcel's address was smudged. {name} took it to the clerk, who found two possible units and no reason to hurry.
{name} caught a supply driver heading toward one of the units. The parcel went along with a note asking for word when it arrived.
A card reached {name}: the parcel had found its owner. The message thanked {him} for returning {gift}, especially with the shortage at home.
A new recruit would not eat with the others. {name} left a place at the end of the bench and said nothing about it.
The recruit sat beside {name} at supper but left before the talk began. {name} passed the bread without trying to start a conversation.
The recruit corrected {name}'s account of a football match. It was the longest sentence anyone had heard from that end of the bench.
At supper, the recruit was arguing about football before {name} arrived. {He} had to ask for room on the bench.
{name} found water collecting beneath the gun's cover. {He} sketched a small shelter and took the drawing to the stores.
The stores supplied {name} with shorter boards than requested. The gun shelter has become an exercise in joints and bad language.
{name} finished the shelter. The crew tested every movement of the gun and discovered that the roof needed moving back a hand's width.
The altered shelter passed inspection. {name} found the crew had added a tiny sign: 'No lodgers'. Someone had already left a blanket inside.
{name} was sent to examine a pump that worked only when struck. {He} asked the men to stop striking it long enough to listen.
The pump's fault proved to be a worn fitting. {name} made a replacement from scrap while the men returned to bailing by hand.
{name}'s replacement fitting held, but the intake kept clogging. {He} fitted a rough screen and stayed through a full shift to watch it.
The pump ran without help. {name} left a short maintenance note and took away the hammer everyone had been using on it.
A patient at the aid post asked {name} for a pencil. By evening, the wall beside the stretcher bore a drawing of a kitchen.
The patient has added a stove and three chairs to the kitchen drawing. {name} asks about each detail while changing the dressing.
Before evacuation, the patient asked {name} to tear the drawing from the paper lining the wall. {He} managed it without losing the stove.
A note arrived from the hospital: the kitchen drawing survived the journey. The patient intends to show the builder exactly where the extra chair should go.
{name} took a wrong turn at two identical trench junctions. {He} decided the route needed names that could be remembered under pressure.
{name} marked the first junction with a spoon and the second with a boot sole. Other runners have begun using the names in their directions.
Someone removed the spoon from {name}'s junction to eat supper. {He} retrieved it and nailed it above comfortable reaching height.
A new runner delivered a message using Spoon Corner and Boot Turn without hesitation. {name} drew both markers on the official route sketch.

mark: a gap beneath a roof beam
a crack in an old stone wall

steps: {name} noticed regular flashes from {mark}. The position looks obvious enough to make {him} suspicious.
{name} watched {mark} through another shift. The flash returns at the same angle, even when nothing else moves.
A second observer helped {name} confirm the trick: a piece of glass, placed to draw fire. The real watching point must be elsewhere.
{name} marked {mark} as a decoy on the observation sketch. {He} passed the warning on and began examining the less obvious gaps.
{name} heard a faint second conversation on the telephone line. Headquarters insisted only one circuit was connected.
The extra voice returned during {name}'s test. It was discussing potatoes, which made enemy intelligence seem an unlikely explanation.
{name} traced the fault to two poorly insulated wires pressed together near a junction. One belonged to the supply office.
With the wires separated, {name}'s telephone carried only orders again. The section misses knowing in advance what is wrong with supper.
{name} obtained a recipe for {dish}. The instructions assume a kitchen, a steady fire and ingredients that do not arrive in sacks.
{name} tried a small batch of {dish}. The bottom burned before the middle cooked. The tasting committee ate the edges and requested patience.
For the second attempt, {name} raised the pot above the hottest part of the fire. The smell brought volunteers before help was requested.
{name} served {dish} to the whole section. Someone asked whether it would appear again. {He} told them to speak to the people delivering the flour.
{name} was asked to arrange a gathering for men who did not want a sermon. {He} asked what they did want and wrote down the answers.
The list for {name}'s gathering contains a poem, a song and a request for five minutes without orders. All three seem possible.
{name} held the gathering in a shelter after supper. The poem was read badly, the song went better, and nobody interrupted the silence.
A man asked {name} to hold another gathering. This time, the request came with a folded poem and an offer to read it.
{name} discovered three men claiming the next place on the leave roster. Each had a different copy of the list.
{name} checked the leave claims against old orders. Two changes had never been copied across; one name had disappeared at a fold in the paper.
The corrected leave list went up under {name}'s signature. Nobody liked every decision, but everyone could see how it had been reached.
The first man left under the corrected roster. {name} watched the departure, then made a second copy of the list before anything else could happen to it.
{name} bought a small phrasebook from a passing soldier. The first useful sentence appears after six pages about hiring a carriage.
{name} practised asking for bread in the local language. The dugout supplied an audience and several confidently incorrect pronunciations.
A local carter understood {name}'s request for bread, then explained that the same sentence sounded very much like a request for a beard.
{name} corrected the phrasebook in pencil. The carter added three useful expressions and refused to translate a fourth suggested by the corporal.
{name} began repairing a blanket with scraps from ruined clothing. The first patch is a different colour from everything else.
Word of {name}'s blanket spread. A strip of lining and a square from an old scarf arrived without explanation.
{name} finished the blanket using six kinds of cloth. The men can identify most of the donors by the patches alone.
The patched blanket kept {name} warm through the night. In the morning, a neighbour arrived with another torn blanket and an optimistic expression.
{name}'s spoon vanished during supper. {He} scratched a mark into a replacement and began keeping a closer eye on the washing bucket.
A second spoon disappeared. {name} searched the washing area and found a gap behind the board where everyone left cutlery to dry.
{name} lifted the board. The gap contained seven spoons, a button and a pencil people had blamed the quartermaster for losing.
The recovered spoons were laid out for collection. {name} took the original and repaired the gap before the next meal.
{name} agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made {him} look twice {his} age.
The artist tried again while {name} read a letter. The new portrait was better, though the ears became the subject of discussion.
{name} sent the portrait home after asking the artist to leave the ears alone. A photograph would have cost more than {he} could spare.
A reply from home thanked {name} for the portrait. It is already on the mantelpiece, where the family apparently recognises the ears.

weather.label: Rain
diary: It rained from dusk to dawn. The communication trenches are knee-deep again and the duckboards float.
Rain all day, steady and patient. The mud has swallowed two more boots and a mule.
Rain found the seams in every roof. Men moved their bedding in small circles, following the last dry patches.
The rain filled yesterday's footprints before the morning carrying parties arrived. Every path had to be learnt again.

weather.label: Fog
diary: Fog sat in the valley until noon. Sentries on both sides fired at shapes that were not there.
A grey wall of fog from dawn to dusk. Patrols went out blind and came back counting each other twice.
Fog erased the landmarks along the front. Orders at trench junctions were repeated at arm's length.
The fog thinned in strips and closed again. Sentries caught brief views of ground they could not keep in sight.

weather.label: Frost
diary: A hard frost. The mud froze into ridges sharp enough to cut boots, and the wire sang in the wind.
Ice on the water in the shell holes. The men stamped their feet all night to keep the blood moving.
Frost stiffened canvas and clothing overnight. Every buckle and knot took longer to work with numb fingers.
Water froze in shallow containers. The first task of the morning was making enough heat to begin the ordinary tasks.

weather.label: Clear
titles: A long view across the wire
diary: A clear, cold day. Good for snipers and observers, bad for everyone else.
Blue sky over the front for the first time in a week. Both sides used it to shell each other with great accuracy.
Clear weather exposed paths usually hidden by haze. Carrying parties waited for darkness rather than risk the open stretches.
The sky stayed clear through the evening. Laundry dried behind the lines while observers watched the roads ahead.

weather.label: Storm
diary: Thunder all night, and nobody could tell which of it was the sky.
A storm broke over the ridge at midnight. Lightning showed the whole front for a heartbeat at a time: wire, craters, men.
The storm drove water sideways beneath the shelters. Loose boards became urgent work, whatever the duty roster said.
Lightning revealed the ground in sudden fragments. Between flashes, the dark seemed thicker than before.

weather.label: Wind
diary: A cold wind from the east carried the smell of the other trenches: smoke, lime and cooking.
Gale all day. Sandbags slid, roofs lifted, and the gas sentries watched the wind direction like hawks.
Wind pulled smoke flat above the trenches. Men checked shelter ropes and kept a close watch on changes in direction.
A hard wind made every loose sheet of metal audible. Conversation moved into doorways and around the sheltered sides of walls.

firstWave: {name} is one of the first hundred to answer the call. {He} wears the ribbon of the First Wave.
Volunteer number {n}. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on {name}'s tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'
{name} was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing {he} owns.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. {name} was number {n}. {He} still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
First Wave. {name} signed when the posters were still wet. {He} keeps the ribbon wrapped in oilcloth with {item}.
{name} answered the first call, number {n} on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on {his} helmet. It has not washed off yet.
{name} was in the first hundred. The old hands in {sector} call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
Number {n} on the early rolls: {name}. The First Wave ribbon arrived with instructions about where to sew it and no needle.
{name} received the First Wave ribbon. {He} checked the stitching twice before putting the tunic back on.
One of the first hundred, {name} was given the First Wave ribbon. {He} wrapped the accompanying paper against the damp.
The First Wave ribbon marked {name} as an early volunteer. At {sector}, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
{name}, volunteer number {n}, received the First Wave ribbon. The quartermaster pronounced the name wrong; {he} corrected it for the record.
The first hundred were recognised, and {name} was among them. {He} wrote the news on the back of an unfinished letter.
{name}'s First Wave ribbon drew a question at supper. {He} remembered the queue at the depot more clearly than the speech.
As one of the first hundred volunteers, {name} received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch.

writes everything down in a tiny notebook
whistles the same four notes over and over
laughs at exactly the wrong moments

a sweetheart who has stopped writing
a wife and a daughter {he} has never met
an old father who runs the family shop alone
a dog called Bastion on the farm
a girl from the dance hall, maybe
five brothers, all on other fronts
a grandmother who prays for both armies
a fiancée who wears {his} ring on a chain
a teacher who said {he} would amount to nothing
twin brothers too young to enlist
a landlady who kept {his} room exactly as it was

{name} came up with a draft of replacements on Day {day}. Nobody asked {his} name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.
The sergeant gave {name} a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day {day} or any other.
{name}, a {trade} from {home}, was sent forward on Day {day} to fill a gap in {sector}. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
"You're late," said the corporal when {name} arrived on Day {day}. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."
{name} arrived with the Day {day} draft, carrying {item} and the news from home, which was old by the time {he} told it.
The old hands of {sector} have been here since Day 1. {name} has been here since Day {day}. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.
{name} walked into {sector} on Day {day} and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
On Day {day} {name} took a post at {sector} that had been empty for two nights. {He} did not ask why. {He} {quirk}, and the men liked {him} for it.
On Day {day}, {name} arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions.
{name} joined the replacements on Day {day}. An old hand checked {his} pack straps before asking {his} name.
Day {day}: {name} reached {sector} with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy.
The draft reached {sector} on Day {day}. {name} was shown which board tipped, which roof leaked and which promises to ignore.
{name} came up on Day {day} carrying news from {home}. A man interrupted to ask whether the railway clock had been repaired.
Day {day}. The corporal put {name} beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
{name} arrived on Day {day} and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
After {daysIn} days of war, {sector} had a place for everything. On Day {day}, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for {name}.

{objective} fell to the {us} at dusk. {name} helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
The {us} flag went up over {objective}. {name} did not cheer. {He} sat down on a sandbag and ate {his} ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Word came down the line: {objective} is ours. {name} shook hands with a corporal {he} had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
{name} walked the captured trenches of {objective} and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. {He} took a spoon as a souvenir.
{objective} is in {us} hands. {name} watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
News that the {us} had taken {objective} reached {name} during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
The {us} secured {objective}. {name} helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that {he} had heard correctly.
Victory at {objective}. {name} let {him}self talk about leave for the first time in days.
The {us} took {objective}, and the orders at {sector} changed before the cheering ended. {name} shouldered another load.
On Day {day}, {objective} passed to the {us}. {name} wrote the name in {his} diary with unusual care.
{objective} has been won. {name} listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
The report confirmed the {us} victory at {objective}. {name} folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
raceLose: Day {day}. {objective} fell to the {them}. {name} watched their flag go up on the heights and dug {his} trench a little deeper.
The {them} hold {objective} now, and they can see straight into {sector}. {name} has learned to walk bent double.
{objective} is lost. {name} heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked {his} rifle twice. There will be another race.
From {objective} the {them} guns have a clear view. {name} wrote to {waiting} that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
The sergeant read out the order: {objective} has fallen, hold the line. {name} looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
The {them} took {objective}. {name} watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
News of the loss of {objective} reached {sector} with the rations. {name} ate while listening to the revised orders.
{objective} is in {them} hands. {name} stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Day {day}: {objective} was lost. {name} wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
The report confirmed that the {them} held {objective}. {name} read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
After the loss of {objective}, {name} helped stack spare sandbags at {sector}. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
The {them} won {objective}. In {sector}, {name} listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
{objective} fell to the {them}. {name} kept the newspaper; {he} wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.
raceHero: The {us} needed one more rifle to take {objective}. {name} was that rifle. From today, they call {him} the Hero of {objective}.
{name} arrived on the very day the {us} reached the heights of {objective}. The men swear {he} tipped the balance. The colonel agreed and wrote it down.
The {us} victory at {objective} made {name} a hero. The men still made {him} wait in the ration queue, which came as a relief.
{name} was named Hero of {objective}. Asked for a few words, {he} gave the names of the people who had helped.
The citation credited {name} with tipping the struggle for {objective}. {He} asked for a copy to send to {home}.
Word spread that {name} had made the difference at {objective}. By evening, the story had grown larger than anything {he} remembered.
{name} became the Hero of {objective}. A recruit asked to shake {his} hand, and neither knew what to say afterwards.
The {us} celebrated {name}'s part in winning {objective}. {He} sat through the praise with a piece of ration bread still in {his} pocket.
The honour for {objective} was read aloud beside {name}. When it was over, someone quietly handed {him} the tea that had been kept warm.
{name} received the title Hero of {objective}. {He} wrote home about it, then added that {he} still needed socks.
transfer: {name} asked to leave the {oldRole}s and serve as a {role}. The sergeant looked at {him} for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.
Orders came through: {name} is a {role} now. {He} handed in {his} old kit and kept only {item}.
{name} transferred to the {role}s. The men in {sector} said they would miss {him}. {He} is only three dugouts away.
After what happened at {place}, {name} asked to serve as a {role}. Nobody argued.
The {role}s took {name} in on a wet morning in {sector}. By noon {he} had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.
{name} reported for duty as a {role}. The new kit was heavier than the explanation of how to use it.
The transfer made {name} a {role}. {He} spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including {him}self.
{name} left the work of a {oldRole} to become a {role}. Someone from the old section came over to see how it was going.
Now serving as a {role}, {name} discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.
{name}'s transfer to the role of {role} was approved. The quartermaster wanted every borrowed item back before issuing anything else.
{name} became a {role} today. {He} wrote the change in a letter home, then crossed out the explanation and tried again.
Orders assigned {name} to work as a {role}. The first lesson began with what not to touch.
The new duty roster listed {name} as a {role}. {He} kept checking the old roster until someone took it down.
exchanged: {name} came back in a prisoner exchange at dawn, thinner, with a borrowed coat and {item}. {He} will not talk about the cage.
A white flag, a handshake in the mud, and {name} walked back across no man's land in an exchange of prisoners. The bay cheered {him} in.
{name} was traded back for an enemy officer. {He} says the other side's coffee is worse than ours, and that is the only thing {he} says.
{name} returned in a prisoner exchange. At the first meal, {he} pocketed half the bread before remembering where {he} was.
The exchange brought {name} back to {sector}. Everyone had questions. The corporal sent them away and fetched a chair.
{name} crossed back during the prisoner exchange with a list of names to pass on. {He} would not rest until someone had copied it.
Returned from captivity, {name} asked for paper before tobacco. There was news that needed to reach {home}.
{name} came back through the exchange with boots that did not match. The quartermaster found a pair without asking for a form.
At the prisoner exchange, {name} recognised a voice before recognising the uniform. {He} finally let go of the bundle under {his} arm.
{name} returned from captivity carrying a spoon worn almost flat. {He} declined a replacement.
The prisoner exchange restored {name} to the rolls. At {sector}, someone had to explain where the dugout had moved.

{He} came back with nothing worse than torn knees.
{He} was back in the bay before the tea went cold.

A grenade fragment found {name}'s shoulder. {He} calls it a souvenir and refuses to be sent back.

bulletCrit: A sniper's bullet hit {name} at {sector}. The medics worked on {him} in the bottom of the trench and shouted for a stretcher.

{name} was propped against the trench wall at {sector}. {He} drank what water the others could spare and stared at the sandbags overhead.
